steps.title: Tailwind 4 writes each colour as lightness, chroma and hue
steps.line: Each line reads oklch(L C h); C, chroma, is distance from grey.

The v4.0 announcement says the move from rgb to oklch makes colours more vivid where sRGB had limited them. This page takes the 300 shade of the 17 coloured families. We will compare each shade with the limits of sRGB and Display P3, then show what the selected screen does when a colour lies outside its range.

steps.title: An sRGB screen’s edge sits at a different chroma for each colour
steps.line: The outline is the most chroma sRGB can show on each spoke.
steps.caption: Each spoke is one family, labelled with its hue. The spokes are evenly spaced; the hues are not: amber to yellow is 7°, red to orange 47°.

steps.title: Tailwind 4 writes each colour as lightness, chroma and hue
steps.line: Each line reads oklch(L C h); C, chroma, is distance from grey.
steps.caption: Tailwind CSS 4.3.3’s theme.css writes all 286 palette shades as oklch(L C h): lightness, chroma (how far from grey) and hue angle. The v4.0 announcement says the move from rgb to oklch makes colours more vivid where sRGB had limited them. This page takes the 700 shade of the 17 coloured families. We will compare each shade with the limits of sRGB and Display P3, then show what the selected screen does when a colour lies outside its range.
steps.picture: Code, 18 lines; 3 labelled values; 2 labels.

steps.title: An sRGB screen’s edge sits at a different chroma for each colour
steps.line: The outline is the most chroma sRGB can show on each spoke.
steps.caption: Each spoke is one family, labelled with its hue. The outline marks the most chroma an sRGB screen can show at that colour’s own lightness and hue, found by bisection with CSS Color 4’s sample code. The spokes are evenly spaced; the hues are not: violet to purple is 9°, yellow to lime 65°.
steps.picture: Radar chart: 1 curve, 17 axes from 0 to 0.35; Key: dark grey, sRGB edge; 7 labels.

steps.title: 14 of the 17 700 shades lie outside sRGB
steps.line: Furthest past the edge: rose-700, by 0.016 chroma.
steps.caption: Tailwind’s own chroma for each colour, drawn over the edge. 14 of 17 lie outside sRGB; only blue, indigo and violet fit. At this scale the overshoot is a sliver: the furthest out in chroma, rose-700, is 0.016 past the edge.

steps.title: As a share of the edge, emerald-700 reaches 111.4%
steps.line: The edge is now the 100 ring; blue has most room, at 84.1%.
steps.caption: The same colours, each as a percentage of the sRGB edge on its own spoke. The edge becomes the 100 ring, and every colour past it shows. emerald goes furthest, to 111.4%; blue has the most room, at 84.1%. The centre is now 50%, and the rings are 25 points apart.

steps.title: None of the 17 lie outside Display P3
steps.line: Closest to the P3 edge: purple-700, at 96.9% of it.
steps.caption: The Display P3 edge on the same scale lies beyond sRGB’s on every spoke, from 101.1% at indigo to 139.5% at green. All 17 colours fit inside it. The closest is purple-700, at 96.9% of the P3 edge, 0.009 chroma short of it.

steps.title: On a Display P3 screen, all 17 show as written
steps.line: Ring 100 is now the P3 edge; sRGB’s falls to 71.7%–98.9% of it.
